Legal Standards.name: Bay-Delta Water Quality Control Plan (WQCP)
Legal Standards.note: California water quality standards for the estuary. Establishes beneficial uses and water quality objectives to protect estuarine ecology, implemented through water-rights requirements affecting flows, salinity, turbidity, and habitat availability.

Legal Standards.name: SWRCB Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641)
Legal Standards.note: Enforceable water-rights conditions implementing Bay-Delta objectives. Principal instrument translating objectives into operational requirements (outflow, export limits, salinity compliance points, DCC operations).

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act water-quality standards framework
Legal Standards.note: Bay-Delta Plan is explicitly framed as CWA water quality standards for the estuary, providing legal backbone for salinity/flow objectives.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Endangered Species Act (ESA) — Section 7
Legal Standards.note: Federal agencies must ensure actions are not likely to jeopardize listed species or adversely modify critical habitat. Implemented through Biological Opinions with operational constraints affecting flows, exports, and habitat conditions.

Legal Standards.name: California Endangered Species Act (CESA)
Legal Standards.note: Prohibits take of state-listed species unless authorized via Incidental Take Permit with minimization/mitigation. Poor ecological conditions can increase take risk and trigger permit compliance issues.

Legal Standards.name: Central Valley Project Improvement Act (CVPIA)
Legal Standards.note: Legally dedicates 800,000 acre-feet annually to fish, wildlife, and habitat purposes, including Bay-Delta protection and ESA obligations.

Legal Standards.name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan coequal goals
Legal Standards.note: Major governing policy mandate: Delta actions evaluated against coequal goals including protecting, restoring, and enhancing the Delta ecosystem.

Tier 1.threshold: Scenario scores in top 25% (low SAV, high turbidity, fresh conditions, expanded microhabitats in most years).

policies.note: Fish and wildlife objectives include salinity, Delta outflow, and export limits.
Compliance is more likely achievable without exceedances when the estuary is consistently fresh and habitat is broadly available.
Lower risk of jeopardy or adverse modification concerns relative to worse tiers because habitat conditions are generally more supportive.
Lower take exposure relative to worse tiers, assuming operations remain within permit conditions where applicable.

Tier 2.threshold: Scenario scores in top 50% (unchanged SAV, high turbidity, fresh conditions, some microhabitats in most years).

policies.note: Objectives are still plausibly met because fresh conditions reduce salinity-objective exceedance pressure.
Operational constraints (exports, outflow targets, gate operations) become binding in dry years to prevent slipping into Tier 3/4 conditions.
If some microhabitats available means frequent bottlenecks in dry sequences, operations may need to tighten to avoid jeopardy or adverse modification risk.
If bottlenecks occur in dry sequences, operators may need to tighten operations to avoid take or habitat degradation.

Tier 3.threshold: Scenario scores in top 75% (unchanged SAV, standard turbidity, moderate salinity, few microhabitats in most years).

policies.note: Moderate salinity and constrained habitat are consistent with conditions where salinity objectives and outflow/export constraints become difficult.
Implements salinity, outflow, and export requirements through project obligations.
Stronger consultation constraints and re-evaluation pressure if operations push habitat conditions toward adverse modification risk.
ITP minimization and mitigation stress where authorized take must be minimized and fully mitigated.
CVPIA (b)(2) water is more likely to be called upon or prioritized to improve conditions because it is dedicated to fish and habitat and to help protect the Delta.

Tier 4.threshold: None of the above; unchanged SAV, low turbidity, moderate to high salinity, few microhabitats in most years.

policies.relationship: Most likely violated / noncompliant (or requiring formal exceptions)
policies.note: Objective exceedances become most plausible here because the Plan's core fish and wildlife protection tools include salinity, Delta outflow, river flows, and export limits.

policies.relationship: Most likely violated / noncompliant (or requiring formal exceptions)
policies.note: Formal noncompliance pathways can become necessary when objectives cannot be met.
Strongest risk that operational regimes could be characterized as causing or contributing to habitat degradation approaching adverse modification or jeopardy.
Heightened likelihood that take risk increases and compliance with minimized and fully mitigated becomes challenging.

policies.policy_name: Delta Reform Act / Delta Plan coequal goals
policies.note: Ecosystem protection mandate becomes sharply implicated because Tier 4 reflects persistent ecosystem degradation relative to the coequal goal of protecting, restoring, and enhancing the Delta ecosystem.
Intensified pressure to deploy (b)(2) water and related restoration measures because the statute explicitly links the dedication to protecting the Delta and meeting ESA obligations.

Governing Agencies.name: SWRCB (State Water Board)
Governing Agencies.note: Sets Bay-Delta Plan objectives; implements via water-rights decisions (notably D-1641) and compliance oversight.

Governing Agencies.name: DWR (CA Dept. of Water Resources)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the State Water Project; must operate to meet applicable SWRCB requirements and other legal constraints (often coordinated with USBR).

Governing Agencies.name: USBR (Bureau of Reclamation)
Governing Agencies.note: Operates the Central Valley Project; implements CVPIA and is a key ESA §7 action agency.

Governing Agencies.name: USFWS & NOAA Fisheries (NMFS)
Governing Agencies.note: ESA consulting agencies issuing BiOps/terms that constrain operations to protect listed species/habitat.

Governing Agencies.name: CDFW (CA Dept. of Fish and Wildlife)
Governing Agencies.note: Administers CESA and incidental take permits; enforces take prohibition.

Governing Agencies.name: Delta Stewardship Council
Governing Agencies.note: Administers the Delta Plan consistency program under the coequal goals framework.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. EPA
Governing Agencies.note: Federal Clean Water Act oversight of water quality standards (as referenced in the Plan’s framing).
